findings.title: toEqual comparisons of Prisma.Sql will fail for SQL built via reduce
findings.body: Three tests assert expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`) against SQL returned by the service. The service builds SQL using a reduce over a Prisma.Sql[] array (insightsBooking.ts lines 119-122, 171-174, 204-207), wrapping each inner Sql with `(${acc}) OR (${condition})` or `(${acc}) AND (${condition})`. Each wrap adds new entries to the inner strings array (one per interpolation point introduced by the wrapper). The expected SQL in the tests is written as a single tagged template literal, producing a Sql whose strings array only has entries at the original placeholders. Prisma's Sql class does not override equality, so Vitest's toEqual does structural comparison of strings and values. For example, the team scope test (line 295) expects strings of length 3, while the service produces strings of length 7 after the OR-reduce wraps the two inner Sql fragments with parens. The same mismatch affects the org scope test at line 332 (3 vs 7) and the combined filter test at line 429 (4 vs 7). The simpler tests pass (NOTHING_CONDITION, user scope, single filter eventTypeId, single filter memberUserId) because they use a single template literal in the service that matches the test literal exactly. Suggested fix: compare conditions.toString() against the expected SQL string, build the expected Sql with the same nested reduce pattern, or assert against actual database query results rather than Sql structure. The PR description already flags that tests were not run due to runner configuration issues, but the structural mismatch will cause these specific tests to fail regardless.

findings.title: findMany method removed without documentation of caller migration
findings.body: The findMany method previously exposed on InsightsBookingService was removed and replaced with getBaseConditions (now at line 68). External callers using service.findMany(...) will no longer compile. The PR description focuses on test updates and does not document this breaking change or describe how existing consumers should migrate to the new pattern of calling getBaseConditions() and passing the resulting Prisma.Sql into prisma.$queryRaw. Before merging, reviewers must confirm there are no remaining callers of service.findMany in the codebase, or that those callers are updated in the same change. Note also that callers using the previously removed type Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput will need to switch to consuming Prisma.Sql directly.
